rationale: I read the complete held EO 13975 (86 FR 6547, signed January 14, 2021, Encouraging Buy American Policies for the United States Postal Service): it sets the Buy American policy for the Postal Service and directs related actions. It has no own term. I read the held full text of EO 14005 (86 FR 7475, signed January 25, 2021, Ensuring the Future Is Made in All of America by All of America's Workers): sec. 14(a) provides 'Executive Order 13788 of April 18, 2017 (Buy American and Hire American), section 5 of Executive Order 13858 of January 31, 2019 (Strengthening Buy-American Preferences for Infrastructure Projects), and Executive Order 13975 of January 14, 2021 (Encouraging Buy American Policies for the United States Postal Service), are hereby revoked.' That names EO 13975 by number, date and title and revokes the whole order; sec. 14(b) supersedes other orders only to the extent inconsistent and does not touch EO 13975. D6 self-check: the OFR note reads 'Revoked by: EO 14006, January 25, 2021' (the history flags the date mismatch). I read the held EO 14006 (86 FR 7483, signed January 26, 2021, Reforming Our Incarceration System To Eliminate the Use of Privately Operated Criminal Detention Facilities): it does not name EO 13975, so the note's order number is an editorial slip for EO 14005, whose date (January 25, 2021) it gives. A search of the held full-run texts for '13975' finds only EO 13975, EO 14005 and an unrelated FR document number in EO 12212; no held later instrument names or restores EO 13975. The single history observation (the API catalog record) was reviewed. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (signing January 25, 2021) is not otherwise adjudicated.
